source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Prime DFW01-01 publishes 20 MW of IT capacity across 213,000 square feet of technical space in Dallas. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 20 MW of IT load is roughly 500 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a density more typical of colocation mixing general enterprise and GPU workloads, the same power supports around 2,000 racks. The operator has not published which density the facility is designed for, so both figures are assumptions, not operator claims. The 213,000 square feet works out to roughly 94 watts per square foot at the published IT capacity, which is consistent with a mixed-use colocation build rather than a purpose-built high-density AI training hall, though that inference is not confirmed by the operator.

SOC 2 Type 2 certifies that the facility's security controls have been independently audited against a defined standard over a period of time, qualifying it to host tenants with data-handling compliance requirements. ISO 27001 certifies that an information security management system is in place against an internationally recognized standard, qualifying it to host tenants with international or enterprise security obligations. Both certifications are published; no tenant names are published.

Within Texas, this site has been mapped alongside 132 other facilities, of which only 13 including this one publish a megawatt figure. Those 13 facilities account for 389 MW of published IT capacity in the state. At 20 MW, Prime DFW01-01 ranks sixth among the facilities this site has read in Texas, representing roughly 5 percent of that 389 MW total. The remaining 120 mapped Texas facilities publish no capacity figure, so the true state total is unknown and 389 MW is a floor, not a ceiling.
